commits.message:
Native Android app (v2.0.0): Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, Capacitor removed

The APK is no longer a WebView wrapper — it's a real native Android app
built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose (the same stack WhatsApp-style
native apps use), wired to the same AttendX backend:

- Login with role picker + OTP forgot-password flow (Gmail SMTP)
- Role-aware bottom-nav workspace (student/faculty/admin)
- Student: dashboard with live attendance %, QR-mark screen using
  CameraX + ZXing with GPS lock and live selfie capture
- Faculty: live session start (geofenced), rotating native QR, live roster
- Admin: people directory from the backend
- Mail Center: raise requests with tracking numbers, track, resolve
- Profile: server URL (cloud or LAN) with test, change password, sign out
- Developer-Options integrity gate on launch (native Settings.Global check)
- Same package + signing key as the WebView build so installs upgrade
  in place without uninstalling

Web fixes alongside: the APK now opens sign-in instead of the web landing
page, and full-height layouts use dvh so everything fits mobile WebViews.
Server update endpoint now derives versionCode as major*10000+minor*100+patch
(1.0.8 -> 10008, 2.0.0 -> 20000) so the update chain stays correct.

Fix app/latest: correct versionCode from patch number, prefer release APK

The update endpoint parsed versionCode from the tag's first digit (v1.0.8 -> 1)
so the in-app update check never fired, and it could hand out the debug APK
when both builds are published. Derive the code from the patch segment and
prefer the signed release asset.

Fix login-page crash, 401 storm, and login layout

  direct grid child that stole the first cell and pushed the form below the
  promo panel (broken two-column layout in screenshots)

commits.message:
Fix server-connection test: use /api/health with 15s cold-start timeout

The test hit /health, which does not exist on the Vercel serverless
mount (only /api/health), and its 4-5s timeout lost to cold starts —
so Test & save always reported "Could not reach the server" against
the deployed URL. Now tries /api/health first with a 15s timeout and
one automatic retry, falling back to /health for standalone LAN servers.

commits.message:
MongoDB migration, OTP mail flows, query tracking, update system, APK hardening

Backend (Express + MongoDB/SQLite):
- Central Gmail SMTP mailer (mailer.ts) powering OTP codes, faculty invite
  codes, attendance-query notifications, and admin mass-mail notices
- OTP password reset: rate limiting, attempt tracking, reset-password endpoint
- Attendance query/complaint system with ATX-Q tracking IDs, public tracking
  endpoint, and student/admin email notifications (queries.ts)
- Faculty verification lifecycle: admin approve -> SMTP invite code -> activation
- Data API rebuilt: auth on reads, boolean/IN/neq filters, relation enrichment
  (classes+schedules, records+session+class), virtual views
  (student_attendance_summary, faculty_assignments, admin_password_reset_queue),
  role-based write rules, settings upsert endpoint
- Attendance integrity: QR nonce replay rejection, device integrity verdicts,
  admin review decisions audit-logged
- App update service: /api/app/latest resolves latest APK from GitHub Releases

Frontend (React):
- Supabase client fully replaced by AttendX API client; Supabase copy removed
- New Attendance Queries view (raise complaint, tracking number, admin queue)
- OTP password reset now completes with a new-password step
- Native detection hardened (WebView UA) so the APK download button never
  shows inside the installed app
- In-app Update banner when a newer APK is published
- Admin Settings: Mass Mail panel with audience picker, recipient count and
  APK-link attachment; boolean settings render as toggles
- Devtools blocking + AttendX-branded console guard on web

Android:
- DeveloperMode plugin adds mock-location (AppOps/provider/setting) and
  USB-debugging detection
- Fixed invalid splash.png (JPEG misnamed as PNG) that broke release builds
- Release signing configured; versionCode 3 (v1.0.3)
- AttendX.apk removed from git; artifacts now ship via GitHub Releases
